sources.ref: Moondrop Custom EQ web app 1.8.0 build 26B1107 (https://hub.moondroplab.com/): device table, per-device configs, EQ editor limits, write sequence

meta.notes: What Moondrop's Custom EQ web app does with the devices it lists outside its main family: it identifies each by USB vendor id 0x35d8 and product id only, never by product name. The ranges are the app's editor limits, not verified firmware limits: 20 to 20000 Hz in whole Hz, gain -18 to +12 dB in steps of 0.1, Q 0.1 to 10 in steps of 0.01, and a pre-gain of -128 to 0 dB in steps of 0.1. The app offers peaking, low and high shelf, low-pass and high-pass filters. The steps here are the grid the device is told: the app rounds gain and pre-gain to 0.1 dB and Q to 0.01 in its editor, then sends each in 1/256ths, so its lowest Q of 0.1 goes out as 26/256. The app computes a pre-gain from the curve and writes it, so the pre-gain is a manual value here. These devices have no Global Gain setting in the app, unlike the main family. Each profile sets its band count and the options that differ from the main family (band frame, commit, custom slot).
